boards.school_name: California Polytechnic State University-San Luis Obispo
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Cal Poly rituals, recurring events, symbols and hands-on practices that connect generations of Mustangs.

cards.title: Start the Mustang Years with WOW
cards.subtitle: Cal Poly’s 60-plus-year welcome tradition
cards.notes: Join the scheduled academic and community-building activities, and use the official orientation program for current participation details.
cards.short_summary: New Mustangs begin their Cal Poly experience through a long-running week of organized orientation activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly identifies Week of Welcome, commonly called WOW, as a tradition more than 60 years old that introduces new students to campus.
cards.access_notes: Participation details and schedules are provided through Cal Poly’s official orientation program.

cards.title: Climb to the Campus P
cards.subtitle: A hillside symbol dating to 1919
cards.notes: Approach the P as an outdoor hike, use established routes and check current university guidance before setting out.
cards.short_summary: The prominent hillside letter doubles as a hiking destination and a canvas for temporary campus messages.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly states that the P was originally constructed in 1919, is a recognized campus symbol and is often decorated to spell messages.
cards.access_notes: The university describes the P as a popular hike; confirm current route conditions and access guidance before visiting.

cards.title: Show Up for Blue-Green
cards.subtitle: Mustangs versus UC Santa Barbara since 1921
cards.notes: Check the official athletics schedule, choose a current Cal Poly–UCSB matchup and support the Mustangs with respectful school spirit.
cards.short_summary: Competition with the UC Santa Barbara Gauchos gives Cal Poly games a century-deep rivalry context.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly documents the Blue-Green Rivalry with UC Santa Barbara and says the schools first met in 1921.
cards.access_notes: Event admission and venue access depend on the selected athletics contest; consult the official schedule.

cards.title: Borrow Einstein’s Exam Luck
cards.subtitle: A pre-exam ritual outside Baker Center
cards.notes: Find the seated Einstein outside Baker Center and gently rub his head before an exam, following the ritual Cal Poly documents.
cards.short_summary: Students turn a campus sculpture into a tactile good-luck stop before tests.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly describes the Einstein statue outside the Baker Center as a photo spot where people rub Einstein’s head for luck before an exam.
cards.access_notes: The statue is outside the Baker Center; respect posted campus access rules and the sculpture.

cards.title: Carry Poly Royal into Open House
cards.subtitle: An annual showcase rooted in a 1933 tradition
cards.notes: Use the official Open House program to select demonstrations and performances that reveal how today’s event carries Poly Royal forward.
cards.short_summary: Cal Poly’s annual campus showcase continues a public-facing tradition that began with Poly Royal.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly says its annual Open House carries on the tradition that began with Poly Royal in 1933 and showcases the university to students, families and the community.
cards.access_notes: Open House is a scheduled annual event; consult the current official program for dates, registration and access.

cards.title: Build Something That Has to Bloom
cards.subtitle: A Cal Poly partnership launched in 1949
cards.notes: Follow the official Rose Float program for public build opportunities and watch students turn engineering and design work into a parade float.
cards.short_summary: Students from the San Luis Obispo and Pomona campuses collaborate on a float for Pasadena’s Rose Parade.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly states that it has designed and built Rose Parade floats with Cal Poly Pomona since 1949.
cards.access_notes: Building and viewing opportunities vary by year; use the official program for current participation information.

cards.title: Build for Design Village
cards.subtitle: A spring tradition in Poly Canyon
cards.notes: Look for the official spring competition schedule and observe the temporary builds alongside generations of experimental student structures.
cards.short_summary: Poly Canyon becomes the setting for an annual competition centered on student-designed structures.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly identifies Poly Canyon as home to generations of student projects and says it hosts the Design Village competition each spring.
cards.access_notes: This is a scheduled spring competition; verify current event and canyon access information before attending.

cards.title: Put Bowling on the Transcript
cards.subtitle: A class taught at Cal Poly’s campus lanes
cards.notes: Search the current class schedule before registration and confirm eligibility if you want the campus bowling-alley experience for academic credit.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus bowling alley allows a recreational pastime to become an enrolled Cal Poly class.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly lists Bowling Class among its traditions and says the campus bowling alley provides an opportunity to take a class for credit.
cards.access_notes: Enrollment and facility use are subject to the current class schedule and Mustang Lanes policies.

cards.title: Finish with a Senior Project
cards.subtitle: The academic rite of passage
cards.notes: Use your department’s current requirements to shape a final project that integrates the knowledge and practical skills developed at Cal Poly.
cards.short_summary: The culminating project turns a student’s accumulated coursework into one final piece of applied work.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly calls Senior Projects a rite of passage that integrates the skills and knowledge students have learned into a final project.
cards.access_notes: Requirements and presentation access vary by academic department; consult the applicable department.

cards.title: Run On with the Pride of the Pacific
cards.subtitle: A marching-band entrance preserved since 1936
cards.notes: Watch for the Mustang Band’s entrance at an official performance, or learn the field tradition through the band if you are an eligible member.
cards.short_summary: The Mustang Band preserves a fast-moving performance custom introduced by director H. P. Davidson.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Mustang Band history says H. P. Davidson established the band’s run-on tradition in 1936 and that it remains in use.
cards.access_notes: Public viewing depends on the current Mustang Band performance schedule; participation is limited to band members.
